cf.title: Report buffer access strategies in EXPLAIN

input.subject: Report buffer access strategies in EXPLAIN

verdict_reasoning: No surviving objection is at level 1a or 1b, and the two that survived at level 2 are fixable. standards-compat-1 asks for the JSON, XML and YAML shape of the property before planned counters and ring size are added. maintenance-fit-1 asks whether 0008 is worth nine index AM call sites when only Bloom reports a non-normal strategy. Both can be settled in the thread without changing the goal.

brief.title: Report buffer access strategies of scan nodes in EXPLAIN
brief.problem: Users and developers cannot see in EXPLAIN whether a scan used normal buffer replacement or a strategy ring meant to limit cache pollution. pg_stat_io shows strategies only per backend and context, with no per plan node attribution. The series also fixes stale buffer README and pg_stat_io text that says strategy I/O happens outside shared buffers.
brief.proposed_design: Table and index scan instrumentation gain an optional bitmask of strategies, which the heap AM and the in-core index AMs fill in; an empty mask means the AM does not report one. EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) prints every strategy seen across rescans, per leader and worker that ran the scan. Sample and TID scans get per worker instrumentation, and patches 0001 to 0003 are documentation fixes that can go in separately.
user_visible_surface: New EXPLAIN property "Buffer Access Strategies:" (for example "normal, bulkread") on Seq, Sample, Bitmap Heap, TID and TID Range Scan nodes.
Same property on Index Scan, Index Only Scan and Bitmap Index Scan nodes; core AMs report normal and Bloom reports bulkread.
Table AM and index AM C API: optional strategy mask in scan instrumentation, with record helpers being renamed to RecordTableScanStrategy() and RecordIndexScanStrategy().
BufferAccessStrategyType moves from bufmgr.h to buf.h.
New glossary entries for the normal, bulkread, bulkwrite and vacuum strategies, plus reworded pg_stat_io context descriptions.
author_claims: Tomas proposed the idea earlier with support from Andres, and Andres agreed to keep the first version to the strategy type only.
Patches 0001 to 0003 are documentation bug fixes, and the README and pg_stat_io fixes could be backpatched.
The work is largely orthogonal to Lukas Fittl's instrumentation work and needs only rebasing.
The feature mostly targets developers and advanced users.
brief.thread_state: Sami Imseih reviewed every version and supports it; Michael Paquier reviewed the documentation patches and Lukas Fittl reviewed v4. Open points: show the property only with VERBOSE (the author agreed), whether 0008 is worth it for Bloom alone, and L2 cache wording awaiting Andres.
unclear: The material does not show v5, so the VERBOSE change and the renames are announced but not posted.
No measurement of EXPLAIN overhead from the added instrumentation.
Index AMs outside core get no stated rule for strategies that change on rescan, beyond keeping every one in the mask.
No reply yet from Andres, Tomas or Melanie, whom Lukas added to the thread.
The material does not say how the property appears in non-text EXPLAIN formats such as JSON.

prior_attempts.title: In bitmap scan explain node show how many relevant heap pages were not examined
prior_attempts.quote: Some of both: it seems like these ought to be consistent, and the lack of complaints so far about regular index-only scans suggests that people don't need the info.
prior_attempts.reason: Tom Lane questioned the need for the counter, because index-only scans report only "Heap Fetches: n" and get no comparable data. He held that the two should be consistent and that the lack of complaints about index-only scans suggests users do not need the information. Amit Kapila marked the entry Returned with Feedback at the end of the commitfest, without further opinions.
prior_attempts.what_is_different: P9 added a counter to Bitmap Heap Scan only, and the objection was that index-only scans had nothing comparable. This series covers table and index scan nodes alike, and the author agreed to show the property only with VERBOSE.

objections.title: Machine-readable EXPLAIN form of the new property is not defined
objections.failure_scenario: A plan visualizer or auto_explain log parser reads EXPLAIN (FORMAT JSON) output. It finds "Buffer Access Strategies" as either a comma-joined string or an array, and per-worker values in a form nobody agreed on. If the shape changes later, for example when ring size or per-strategy counters are added, these tools break after an upgrade.
objections.argument: The text sample "normal, bulkread" is the only form shown, and the documentation hunks in 0007 and 0008 describe only text output. Message #6 and message #8 already plan per-strategy buffer counters as the next step, and message #5 plans ring size, so the key and value shape chosen now must allow those additions. The VERBOSE gating agreed in message #19 is not posted yet, so the visible contract is still the v4 default output.
objections.author_must_show: What key name and value type does the property have in JSON, XML and YAML, for the leader and for each worker, and how will later counters fit without changing that shape?

critic.reasoning: The thread and the documentation hunks in 0007 and 0008 show only the text form. Messages #5, #6 and #8 plan ring size and per-strategy counters, so the JSON key and value type are a fair thing to settle now.

objections.title: Index AM strategy hooks add nine call sites for one contrib case
objections.failure_scenario: A later patch makes nbtree or GIN use a bulkread ring on some new path but does not call RecordIndexScanStrategy() there. EXPLAIN keeps printing "normal" for that scan. No test fails, and a developer chasing cache pollution trusts the wrong value until someone reads the AM code.
objections.argument: 0008 places strategy recording in every in-core index AM, at nine call sites (message #19). Today only Bloom reports anything other than normal. Lukas questioned whether 0008 adds value (message #19 quotes him), and the author agreed that Bloom alone may not justify it. Each future strategy change in any index AM, in core or out of core, must now remember this call, and nothing checks that it does.
objections.author_must_show: Which index AM, other than Bloom, is expected to select a non-normal strategy, and how would a missed RecordIndexScanStrategy() call be detected?

critic.reasoning: Message #19 confirms nine call sites and that Bloom is the only in-tree index AM reporting a non-normal strategy. The proposal names no check that catches a missed record call, and the author concedes Bloom alone may not justify 0008.

refuted.title: More parallel worker instrumentation code ahead of a planned rework
refuted.failure_scenario: 0006 copies the DSM estimate, init, attach and retrieve code into Sample and TID scans. Lukas's parallel instrumentation rework then has two more nodes to convert. A missed node drops worker-only strategies from EXPLAIN, which is the same bug Sami found in v1, and it shows up only under debug_parallel_query.
refuted.argument: The author agrees that 0006 extends existing duplication and defers the cleanup (message #19). Lukas has an unposted patch set that reworks parallel worker instrumentation reporting (message #12). The v1 SampleScan bug in message #2 shows that per-node worker plumbing breaks without notice. [P24] records a revert of a new EXPLAIN counter because of failures under debug_parallel_query.
refuted.author_must_show: Could 0006 wait for, or be built on, Lukas's parallel instrumentation rework instead of adding two more copies of the per-node DSM code?

precedents.title: Revert "Show index search count in EXPLAIN ANALYZE."

critic.reasoning: Lukas, who owns the unposted rework, wrote in message #12 that he sees no immediate problems, and in message #13 that 0006 seems fine. 0006 copies the pattern of three existing nodes, and [P24] records a test failure in another feature.

refuted.title: No user report shows a need for per-node strategy in EXPLAIN
refuted.failure_scenario: A DBA sees "Buffer Access Strategies: bulkread" on a Seq Scan and has no setting to change it, because the heap AM chooses the ring from table size. The property is then read mostly by developers, while table AM and index AM authors keep filling the mask for good.
refuted.argument: The demand in the material is support from developers (Tomas, Andres, Sami) and one conference question about rings, which is a documentation issue that 0003 already fixes. Lukas says users have little control over the strategy and calls this mostly for developers in message #13, and the author agrees in message #19. Per-backend counters by context already exist in pg_stat_get_backend_io (message #7). [P9] was returned partly because missing complaints suggested users did not need a similar EXPLAIN counter.
refuted.author_must_show: Which real tuning or diagnosis case did per-node strategy reporting solve that pg_stat_io or pg_stat_get_backend_io could not?

precedents.title: In bitmap scan explain node show how many relevant heap pages were not examined

critic.reasoning: A DBA seeing a property with no setting to change it is not a failure, and pg_stat_get_backend_io cannot attribute per plan node. Several developers back the feature and the author agreed to VERBOSE only; [P9] was about consistency with index-only scans.

refuted.title: Index scan reporting (0008) adds AM-wide hooks for one Bloom case
refuted.failure_scenario: Every in-core index AM gets a record call, nine call sites in total, and out-of-core AMs inherit a new optional duty. Almost every Index Scan then prints "normal". Only Bloom full-index scans show anything else, so nearly all of the cost buys nothing visible.
refuted.argument: Message #19 says Bloom is the only in-tree index AM that uses bulkread. It also says this single case "might not be enough to justify 0008". Lukas questions the value of 0008 in message #13, and the thread has not settled the point. The cost spreads across nbtree, hash, GiST, GIN, SP-GiST and BRIN, plus the instrumentation API.
refuted.author_must_show: Which index AM, in core or as an extension, besides Bloom picks a non-normal strategy, and who needs to see that in EXPLAIN?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of maintenance-fit-1, which makes the same point about 0008 and Bloom and adds a concrete scenario of a missed record call.

touch_points.label: ABI / extension API
touch_points.reason: Table and index scan instrumentation gain a strategy mask, and BufferAccessStrategyType moves from bufmgr.h to buf.h.

touch_points.label: SQL-standard conflict or non-standard syntax
touch_points.reason: see objection standards-compat-1: Machine-readable EXPLAIN form of the new property is not defined

touch_points.label: psql UX conventions
touch_points.reason: EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) prints a new "Buffer Access Strategies" property on table and index scan nodes.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: The author proposes to backpatch the README and pg_stat_io documentation fixes in 0001 and 0003.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: 0008 adds record calls in every in-core index AM, and 0006 adds per-worker DSM code to Sample and TID scans.

touch_points.label: performance on the hot path
touch_points.reason: 0005 and 0008 touch heapam.c and the index AM search paths; recording is requested only when buffer instrumentation is on.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: What key name and value type does the property have in JSON, XML and YAML output, for the leader and for each worker?
How will the planned ring size and per-strategy counters fit into that output without changing its shape?
Which index AM other than Bloom is expected to select a non-normal strategy, in core or as an extension?
How would a missed RecordIndexScanStrategy() call in a new index AM code path be detected?
What does EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) cost with the added instrumentation, compared with master, on a plan with many scan nodes?

committability.owner_note: Michael Paquier reviewed only the documentation patches. 0004 to 0008 need someone who knows the buffer manager and the executor's parallel instrumentation code; Andres, Tomas and Melanie were added to the thread but have not replied.
committability.liability: The owner signs for a new EXPLAIN property in all output formats, an optional strategy mask in the table AM and index AM instrumentation API, and per-worker DSM code for Sample and TID scans. External EXPLAIN parsers depend on the key and value shape from the first release.
committability.author_follow_up: The author answered each review within days, posted four versions, and announced a v5 with the VERBOSE change and the renames.

priority.reason: The author states that the feature mostly targets developers and advanced users. The series is eight patches across explain.c, heapam.c, the executor scan nodes and all in-core index AMs, but 0001 to 0003 are separate documentation fixes and the remaining open points are small.

provisional_note: The code and v5 were not read, so the VERBOSE gating, the non-text output shape and the cost of the recording calls in heap and index AM paths are unchecked. The parallel worker handling in 0006 is also unjudged.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Eagerly evict bulkwrite strategy ring
precedents_retrieved.summary: Make the BAS_BULKWRITE buffer access strategy flush several dirty buffers in its ring at once, skipping buffers whose flush would require a WAL flush. This was meant as a first step toward combining writes and issuing them asynchronously, and gave about 15-20% faster parallel COPY FROM.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author withdrew the entry after moving all of its patches into the patch set in the separate write combining thread, so the work continues there. No reviewer objected to the design; reviews found only code issues, which the author fixed. Earlier the author noted that the gain from this patch alone might not justify committing it.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: All of the patches that implement the bulkwrite eager flush functionality are included in the patch set being actively updated in this thread [1] on write combining.

precedents_retrieved.title: explain_regress, explain(MACHINE), and default to explain(BUFFERS)
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch series adds a GUC explain_regress, set on by pg_regress, that turns off TIMING, SUMMARY, COSTS and BUFFERS, so that BUFFERS can become the default for EXPLAIN without changing regression output. An optional explain(MACHINE) option hides machine-dependent EXPLAIN ANALYZE output such as memory use, sort details and Heap Fetches.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane objected that making EXPLAIN behave differently for developers and tests than for users may cause confusion and hide bugs. He also noted that the GUC had no documentation, that MACHINE is an unclear option name, that the GUC is not applied under make installcheck, and that the postgres_fdw change can break older postgres_fdw versions talking to new servers. The author then suggested closing the entry until someone finds another way to enable BUFFERS by default.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Making
EXPLAIN work significantly differently for developers and test
critters than it does for everyone else seems likely to promote
confusion and hide bugs.

precedents_retrieved.title: Implement TODOs for index operator strategy number validation
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds strategy number bounds checks to operator class validation for BRIN, GIN, GiST and SP-GiST, implementing TODOs in that code. BRIN and SP-GiST use RTMaxStrategyNumber as the upper limit, GiST uses a limit computed from the Geo* constants, and GIN keeps its existing limit of 63.
precedents_retrieved.objection: GiST, SP-GiST and BRIN set amstrategies = 0, so strategy numbers are defined by each opclass, and the new checks would make amvalidate() reject valid custom opclasses. RTMaxStrategyNumber is not a general limit for these access methods, and the Geo* constants apply only to the built-in GiST point implementation. The author withdrew the patch for rework.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
For example, a custom SP-GiST opclass can use strategy 31 if its support
functions understand it, but this patch would make amvalidate() reject
it.

precedents_retrieved.title: explain: show JIT details in non-text format, even if zero
precedents_retrieved.summary: Change EXPLAIN so that in non-text output formats (YAML, XML, JSON) the JIT section is always printed when JIT instrumentation exists, even if no functions were JIT-compiled, so that the keys stay present with zero values. The patch relaxed the early return in ExplainPrintJIT to apply only to text format.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Peter Eisentraut saw no point in the change, arguing that when JIT is explicitly turned off there is no need to clutter EXPLAIN output with zeroes. Tom Lane found that the JIT control GUCs are consulted only at plan time, so the only run-time cases are setting jit=off between planning and execution or failing to load the JIT provider; on that basis he agreed it was not worth changing. The author, who had said he had no personal need for the patch, then withdrew it.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
On balance I agree with Peter's opinion that this isn't worth
changing.  I would be for the patch if the executor had a little
more freedom of action, but as things stand there's not much
freedom there.

precedents_retrieved.title: New strategies for freezing, advancing relfrozenxid early
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch series lets each VACUUM choose a skipping strategy and a freezing strategy at the start, using a snapshot of the visibility map, so that unfrozen all-visible pages do not pile up until an aggressive VACUUM. A new vacuum_freeze_strategy_threshold GUC and reloption, default 4GB, makes VACUUM freeze eagerly in tables above that size, and a further patch avoids allocating new MultiXactIds during freezing.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Andres Freund posted a short test with transient data, cited in message #98, in which autovacuum wrote about 1.5x to 7x as much WAL with eager freezing. He argued that table size cannot tell VACUUM whether eager freezing is a good idea, and said he saw no alternative to reverting the commit. Robert Haas agreed that the scenario is common and objected to large behavior changes based on limited evidence. Peter Geoghegan reverted the commit and withdrew the whole series.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: The actual scenario he came up with is three lines of SQL, and it's nothing remotely obscure. That kind of thing is going to happen *all the time*.

precedents_retrieved.title: In bitmap scan explain node show how many relevant heap pages were not examined
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds an "unfetched" count under "Heap Blocks" in EXPLAIN ANALYZE for Bitmap Heap Scan, next to "exact" and "lossy", for heap pages that the visibility map let the bitmap-only scan skip. The author also suggested renaming the node to "Bitmap Only Heap Scan" but did not implement it.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane questioned the need for the counter, because index-only scans report only "Heap Fetches: n" and get no comparable data. He held that the two should be consistent and that the lack of complaints about index-only scans suggests users do not need the information. Amit Kapila marked the entry Returned with Feedback at the end of the commitfest, without further opinions.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Some of both: it seems like these ought to be consistent, and the
lack of complaints so far about regular index-only scans suggests
that people don't need the info.

precedents_retrieved.title: Show WAL stats on pg_stat_io
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds WAL I/O (writes, fsyncs, reads during recovery, and WAL segment initialization in a new IOCONTEXT_INIT) to the pg_stat_io view as IOOBJECT_WAL. Timings use track_wal_io_timing, and pg_stat_wal timings would come from pg_stat_io.
precedents_retrieved.objection: pg_stat_io ties op_bytes to a fixed block size per object and context, but some WAL reads, such as those by the WAL receiver, have a variable size. Reviewers did not agree whether to set op_bytes to 1, to NULL, or to add per-operation byte columns. Michael Paquier proposed to set the patch aside until WAL reads and writes, async I/O and cached reads are settled, so that the meaning of pg_stat_io does not change between releases. The author agreed, and the patch was marked Returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
IMHO, perhaps we'd better put this patch aside until we are absolutely
*sure* of what we want to achieve when it comes to WAL, and I am
afraid that this cannot happen until we're happy with the way we
handle WAL reads *and* writes, including WAL receiver or anything that
has the idea of pulling its own page callback with
XLogReaderAllocate() in the backend.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert "Show index search count in EXPLAIN ANALYZE."
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "Show index search count in EXPLAIN ANALYZE."
Reverted commit(s): Show index search count in EXPLAIN ANALYZE.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit 5ead85fbc81162ab1594f656b036a22e814f96b3.

This commit shows test failures with debug_parallel_query=regress.  The
underlying issue needs to be debugged, so revert for now.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent records rejecting this idea. P9's demand argument is weakened here: support from Tomas and Andres is reported (message #1), and output moves to VERBOSE (message #19). P24's revert reason is a test-level risk, outside levels 1-2.

Default-output noise was raised in message #13, and the author agreed to VERBOSE gating in message #19. The strategy names reuse the existing pg_stat_io context values. Only the non-text format contract remains open from this angle.

The series adds no persistent or cross-node state: no on-disk format, WAL record, catalog, wire-protocol or replication change. The strategy mask lives in per-query executor instrumentation and parallel DSM, so it exists only inside one server version. The struct changes and the move of BufferAccessStrategyType to buf.h target master (v20) only, and only the doc patches 0001 to 0003 are proposed for backpatch. The nbtree VACUUM bookkeeping invariant does not apply, because nbtsearch.c only records the scan strategy and leaves no state for a later VACUUM pass.

The proposal has no privilege or exposure aspect. EXPLAIN ANALYZE already requires the user to run the query, and the new property shows only which buffer replacement policy that user's own scan picked; this follows from table size versus shared_buffers, which pg_class and pg_settings already show.
The nbtree VACUUM bookkeeping invariant does not apply, because 0008 only records a scan strategy in nbtsearch.c. Patches 0001 to 0003 are documentation fixes and raise no maintenance concern.

No existing feature gives per plan node strategy attribution. pg_stat_io and pg_stat_get_backend_io() count I/O per backend and context, and the author answered this in message #7. The heap rule for choosing bulkread is not documented for users, and it changes across rescans (message #4). No extension or contrib module that reports this is known to me, and a hook would not be cheaper than extending the existing scan instrumentation. Whether the property earns its place, given that most nodes print normal, is a desirability question for another angle (message #13).
Patches 0001 to 0003 fix stale documentation and need no demand case. The objections above apply only to the EXPLAIN reporting in 0004 to 0008.
